shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses turn on the same word for its end/latter part -- וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ (oshb:Prov.14.12) and וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ (oshb:Prov.14.13), byte tier -- functioning both times as the pivot from an opening observation to its outcome: a way that seems right before a man, but its end is the ways of death (14:12); even in laughter a heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief (14:13). The repeated hinge-word is not incidental vocabulary here -- it is the word each verse's own point depends on, which is why these two verses read as a matched pair rather than as two unrelated observations that happen to share a term. A second, independently named ground supports the pairing alongside the hinge-word: both verses share the identical appearance-vs-outcome template (what seems/is X in the moment ends in Y), naming the shared structure rather than resting the pairing on the hinge-word alone.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping these as two separate rows was considered, since both verses are grammatically complete on their own; the pair was adopted instead because the shared hinge-word is the operative word of both verses' arguments, not a passing vocabulary overlap, giving it more weight than the one-token catchword pairs at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 and Prov.13.19-Prov.13.20. The identical proverb recurs verbatim at Prov.16.25 (byte tier); that duplicate is disclosed as counter-evidence for any claim of a construction unique to this seam, though it does not by itself unseat the pairing argued here.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry the bare word for 'to/of his neighbor' -- לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ (oshb:Prov.14.20, byte tier) and לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ (oshb:Prov.14.21, byte tier) -- both governing the verse's central claim about how the poor are treated: even to his neighbor a poor person is hated, while those who love a rich person are many (14:20); one who despises his neighbor sins, but one who is gracious to the needy is called happy (14:21). shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The two verses share the noun ruach in the same 'haughty/lowly of spirit' slot: רֽוּחַ (oshb:Prov.16.18, 'height of spirit') and ר֭וּחַ (oshb:Prov.16.19, 'lowly of spirit'), and they share the pride root as well: גָּא֑וֹן (oshb:Prov.16.18, 'pride') and גֵּאִֽים (oshb:Prov.16.19, 'the proud'). Two shared roots in consecutive verses turn the famous pride-before-a-fall line and the lowly-spirit saying that follows it into a bound pair. The inventory records a ketiv/qere note at Prov.16.19: an inline ketiv עניים precedes the qere עֲנָוִ֑ים.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 16:18 as its own well-known proverb was the initial draft; the pairing was adopted once both the ruach and the ge'ah/ga'on root were confirmed shared with 16:19 rather than assumed from familiarity with the verse alone.

shipped_row.device_notes: 16:18 is synonymous (staircase) parallelism; 16:19 is antithetic (lowly spirit with the poor versus dividing plunder with the proud); the ketiv/qere crux at 16:19 is the reason this cluster's confidence sits lower than the 16:12-16:15 run.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The highway of the upright is to turn from evil; whoever keeps his way preserves his life; the verse restates one path-image in two clauses rather than opposing two subjects.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A cluster with 16:18 sharing a loose pride/downfall theme was considered and dropped: the two verses share no repeated root.

next_row.boundary_rationale: One who heeds the word finds good, and whoever trusts in YHWH is blessed; the verse pairs two synonymous conditions of well-being rather than opposing them.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A join back to 16:19 on the shared tov root — ט֣וֹב (oshb:Prov.16.19, opening-comparative slot) and ט֑וֹב (oshb:Prov.16.20, clause-object slot) — was tried and dropped: 16:19 uses its tov as the opening comparative of an antithetic verse, 16:20 as the object of its opening clause, and no other token is shared across 2 verses; the ruach/pride-root pairing that runs through 16:18-19 (שְׁפַל ר֭וּחַ / גֵּאִֽים, oshb:Prov.16.19, echoing גֹּ֣בַהּ רֽוּחַ / גָּא֑וֹן, oshb:Prov.16.18) does not carry over into this verse either.
